Tammy Taylor 3

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Fake nails, fake products, fake labels - is this the end of the road for Mel and Peet Viljoen and the South African franchise of Tammy Taylor Nails?

Unique Selling Point:
Documentary evidence that Peet & Mel Viljoen are no longer License Holders for Tammy Taylor Nails, and that their Distribution Agreement has not been renewed. However, they still have 40+ Tammy Taylor Salons operating in Southern Africa, which are now infringing on the Tammy Taylor trademark which is registered to Tammy Taylor Inc. (A company registered in the USA). Not only are their investments and their livelihoods at stake, but they are knowingly or unknowingly selling fake products which have not been procured from Tammy Taylor USA.
For the past year Mel & Peet Viljoen have been importing products (gels. powders, etc) from the Netherlands, and bottles and containers from China. These are then re-branded with Tammy Taylor labels printed in Pretoria. We have invoices proving the purchase as well as a video of Mel examining a peeling fake label.

Summary:
Peet Viljoen also contracted with Tahera Mather (Digital Vibes) to supply 80 000 face masks to the Department of Health and 20 000 to SAPS in 2020. He was paid R5.1 million for these by Spin Wizards, a company implicated in the Digital Vibes saga which saw the former Minister Zweli Mkhize stepping down. Peet then made a big splash in every local newspaper about donating 1000 masks to the police. Masks paid for handsomely by the Department of Health's communication budget.
The SIU Report also details how R650 000 of this budget was diverted to Minister Mkhize's daughter-in-law to open a new Tammy Taylor Nail salon in Pietermaritzburg's Midlands Mall.

Further information:
Entrepreneur and influencer Happy Simelane paid R2.8 million for the Tammy Taylor Menlyn Maine store in August 2021. She was presented with a set of fake financials by Peet, drawn up by his 'accountant'. This shows the monthly rental as R21 000 per month. In reality the rental is R62 597 per month. Happy never received a set of keys to the shop, and the business was only transferred into her name on 12 October 2021. Nevertheless she received a letter of demand from Peet for 2 months rental (September & October 2021) totalling about R150 000. According to the franchise agreement if the rental is 2 months in arrears they can take back the store. Which they did, and Happy lost her R2.8 million.
In addition to this her husband was killed in a car accident in June this year. She is taking them to court.

TAMMY TAYLOR 3


V/O: On the 20th of October two policemen arrived at our producer’s gate in Johannesburg.

Motau: Are you Kate Barry?

Kate: I am.

Motau: Do you work for what you call – Carte Blanche?

Kate: That’s right.

Motau: We are here to serve a Protection Order here to serve.

V/O: It soon became clear that something else was at play: a blatant act of intimidation; a brazen attempt to interfere with our investigation into a company you may have seen before.

V/O: Two years ago Carte Blanche exposed the dodgy dealings of
Tammy Taylor Nails South Africa – a business with 46 franchise stores.

Taryn: It’s derailed my entire life.

Ntombi: I feel like I’m about to lose everything that I’ve invested.

Daniella: It was the worst experience of my life.

V/O: The real Tammy Taylor is an American entrepreneur who founded a brand of superior nail products in 1983. The local franchisors were two colourful but compromised characters: Mel Viljoen and her husband Peet.

Peet: Hi, I’m Peet Viljoen.

V/O: Peet Viljoen is a disbarred lawyer who was struck off the roll by the Pretoria High Court in 2011.
Local Tammy Taylor franchisees had lost millions when stock was withheld, refunds were withheld and their stores were simply confiscated and resold. But Mel Viljoen was unapologetic.

Mel: We’re going to keep selling franchises, we’re going to keep taking over stores if people don’t pay their fees. That is just the way business is.

V/O: A year later we were back. This time Tammy Taylor in the USA was intending to terminate the Master License Agreement. The Viljoens denied this, claiming the email was forged. After our last story, one case study “Jessica” received some of her money back but is still waiting for a full refund.

V/O: You may have thought it ended there, but shocking new information has now come to light. We were sent anonymous emails with hard evidence. Insiders approached us eager to expose the truth – and so here is the real reality show of Mel and Peet Viljoen.

Happy Simelane is a successful businesswoman who bought the Tammy Taylor Menlyn Maine store in July last year for R2.8 million cash.

Happy: They told me I will be making between 300 and 500K monthly and that sold me. They gave me the financials and yeah, it was very convincing. So as a businessperson, for me that made sense you know. Only to find out even the financials don't… I don't think they’re like legit.

V/O: The financial statements they gave her were for a company with this name, with this registration number, trading as Tammy Taylor Menlyn Maine.

But the business they registered in her name was this company called Menlyn Maine (Pty) Ltd – a shelf company with a different registration number and no financials. This suggests she didn’t get the company she paid for.

They claimed the monthly rental was just over R21 000. But the actual rental is over R70 000 as bank statements prove.

Masa: And when did you get your store?

Happy: Did I ever get my store? I don’t have a store. There was a handover document that they made me sign to say okay, we are handing over the salon to you on the 1st of September. The company was never in my name which made it very difficult for me to open a bank account.

V/O: Happy signed a handover document that stipulates should the rental be in arrears for more than 60 days while the lease agreement is in the name of Melany Viljoen, the salon may be reclaimed by Tammy Taylor Nails head office without any refund.

Happy: I was never given access to the bank account, or even have a key to say Happy this is your store.

V/O: This means that all the store’s earnings were going into a bank account controlled by Head Office.

Masa: When you confront Mel and Peet what do they say?

Happy: You know Mel will always say I don’t know, I don’t know. She was the director of Menlyn Maine and she had to resign and appoint me. They only did that 12 October.

V/O: But Happy was responsible for all salon expenses from the 1st of September, so the 6 weeks delay in transferring the business into her name, meant she couldn’t control what was being spent.

Happy: Then they started sending me a letter of demand for the rent that they paid in September.

V/O: On the 22nd of October the Viljoens sent Happy a letter of demand for over R152 000, claiming she was in arrears on 2 months rental.

Happy: It doesn’t make sense, why must I pay for that 2 months rental while they’ve got access to the account? They’re the ones using and misusing the funds in that same account, and they’re misusing the funds deliberately so that I will be left with nothing.

V/O: This meant she was now in breach of the handover agreement she’d signed, which meant the Viljoens could reclaim the store. In a written response to Carte Blanche Mel Viljoen states:

We have not done or taken anything that Happy did not agree to in writing. Sadly, Happy did not honor her agreement with the brand. Happy Simelane were given ampule time to remedy her breach. (sic)

Link: This was supposed to be Happy Simelane’s salon, but after paying R2.8 million in cash, in full, she didn’t even get the keys to the store. The Viljoens took her money and then tried to sell the store to the next buyer.

Happy: This is what they do for a living, and you know Peet is just hungry for blood, he’s just going after our money and he’s doing it deliberately and he’s enjoying it. And he thinks he’s untouchable. I want to tell Peet right now you’ve messed with the wrong one.

Link: Peet Viljoen will tell anyone who will listen that the R345 000 franchise licence fee is fully refundable. But that’s simply not true. You will not get your refund, well not without a struggle. And if you don’t believe me then listen to Peet Viljoen himself in these astonishing voice recordings were sent to Carte Blanche anonymously.

Peet: I don’t think I’ve given back a license fee yet. Mel has behind my back…

V/O: These recordings expose Peet’s true nature. Speaking to someone called Lorraine, he admits the promised refund is just a sales pitch.

Lorraine: Must you do that?

Peet: That’s how they buy, Lorraine.

Lorraine: Hmmm?

Peet: That’s how they buy.

Lorraine: Because they think it’s refundable?

Peet: Yes!

V/O: He then lashes out at Lorraine for disagreeing.

Peet: Fucking bitch, you sell it for me non-refundable!

Lorraine: I’m just saying…

Peet: No, no please, you’re smart. Give her two sales today, see if she can do it non-refundable. Tell them so.

V/O: He goes on to explain his modus operandi.

Peet: Right, now I’m going to change one thing that totally puts you, once again in fuck you check mate – it’s the following: when we go from that agreement to this one hey, then when you sign it, it is “no refund”.

Peet: Refund expires. But now it’s a contract. And that’s the shit that these dumb, fucking people don’t understand.

V/O: But that’s not where the deception ends as our investigation reveals.

Link: This is Mel Viljoen’s application for a Protection Order – a desperate attempt to intimidate the media. She asked the court to prohibit Carte Blanche from airing or interviewing or contacting anyone relating to her or her company. The court did not issue the order, yet the Viljoens are claiming that it did.
Now if you’ll go to these lengths to try and gag Carte Blanche you probably have something to hide.

V/O: Since the Master License Agreement was cancelled the Viljoens have no right to use the name. Tammy Taylor US sent them a Cease & Desist notice, so why have they continued selling franchises and products? We asked both Peet and Mel for an interview, but they referred us to this press release:

“The company owned by Melany Viljoen registered the trademark in South Africa. The South African courts do not recognise American law, and the trademark shall remain the property of Melany Viljoen until a South African court rules otherwise.”

But that is a lie.

V/O: Karel Bredenkamp is a patent attorney specialising in intellectual property.

Karel: A company called Just Smart Mobile registered six trademarks for the name Tammy Taylor, or really for logos and including the name Tammy Taylor in the logos. And this was done in June 2016.

V/O: Just Smart Mobile belongs to Mel Viljoen. But in 2018 she signed over all her rights to these trademarks to Tammy Taylor US as this Deed of Assignment proves.

Karel: So these applications that were filed by Just Smart are now in the name of Tammy Taylor Nails Inc. – in other words the US company.

V/O: Tammy Taylor Inc now owns 11 South African trademark registrations and Mel Viljoen owns none.

Karel: From this you can see that Tammy Taylor US then filed the word mark – or just the name, the words Tammy Taylor – un-stylized, not as a logo, just Tammy Taylor – and then they also file three logos.

Link: Everything you see here from the name, the logo, the products, is Intellectual Property. And it’s the Intellectual Property of Tammy Taylor Incorporated, a company registered in the United States of America. Now since the Master License Agreement between Tammy Taylor US and the Viljoens has been cancelled all of this is a trademark infringement.

Karel: The franchisees are exposed. I would strongly suggest that they contact Tammy Taylor US to get authorization again to use the trademarks.

V/O: The Distribution Agreement was cancelled in April and Tammy Taylor US no longer supplies the Viljoens. So what fake products are they using?

Keystone Cosmetics is an American company, manufacturing nail products at their factory in New Jersey. Their European office is based in the Netherlands, and it’s from here the Viljoens are buying generic products. Here’s an invoice for over 5000 Euros of gels and powders from Keystone Cosmetics. They order through Mel Viljoen’s company called Nectacraft, the same company that was ordering authentic Tammy Taylor products. We called Keystone’s local representative Yvonne to ask about this order.

Masa: Are you aware that Nectacraft is actually Tammy Taylor Nails?

Yvonne: I don’t answer these types of questions because all our customers are confidential.

V/O: An insider revealed the Viljoens are also importing bottles and jars and then rebranding them with fake Tammy Taylor labels.

Link: This is an authentic Tammy Taylor Nail Kit from 3 years ago. This is the real thing – manufactured, packaged and labelled in the United States. Everything has got the tammytaylor.com website on it.

V/O: But now some of the labels show dot co dot za, while others are clearly not up to scratch as Mel points out to her staff in this leaked video.

Mel: The printing is coming off quite hectically. It’s so bad that you can just do this and then, look there!

V/O; In another leaked video she places authentic Tammy Taylor jars in front of the fake jars that need labelling.

Mel: Please don’t remove these jars that I’ve put there until we’ve got our stickers, otherwise you won’t know what it is. Okay?

V/O: So where are labels being printed? Our investigation led us to this warehouse in Midrand.

Masa: We just wanted to know did you print these labels, does that artwork look familiar?

Guy: Ja, the artwork does look familiar. I’m not sure if it’s the exact artwork because they sent a lot of iterations of it, but we have printed something similar to this.

V/O: Further investigation led us to this industrial park in Pretoria. The owner of the Marvel Group showed us some work he’s done for Tammy Taylor.

Rudy: Basically what we do is they send us the artwork and we print directly onto the bottles.

Masa: Ah, but you see what it says here. You know it still says made in the USA?

Rudy: Yeah.

Masa: I mean this is not the USA?

Rudy: No, not at all.

Karel: Well that amounts to trademark infringement, and it also constitutes counterfeiting, because it’s not a product that emanates from Tammy Taylor US.

Masa: Just to be clear on this Karel, this is all illegal?

Karel: It's all illegal. Counterfeit products could be confiscated and destroyed.

V/O: That brings us back to the policemen who arrived at our producer’s gate.

Kate: And can I see the other side please?

Motau: Which side?

Kate: Mr Motau? Oh, Mr Motau which police station are you from?

Motau: From Garsfontein.

Kate From Garsfontein?

Motau: Yes.

V/O: Detective Motau is from Pretoria. Sources confirm he was at Tammy Taylor Head Office when a disgruntled franchisee was arrested last year. We played him this video and Motau confirmed he’s the one in the green shirt. But why would this same officer keep turning up? Insiders allege he’s moonlighting.

Motau: Alleged?

Kate: Yes alleged.

Motau: Alleged.

Kate: Yes.

Motau: You don’t have anything, any proof of anything?

Kate: No, it’s alleged. That’s what people do, they make allegations, so I’m asking you.

Motau: Those are serious allegations.

Kate: Yes, so I’m asking is it true or is it not true? That’s all.

Motau: No comment.

V/O: During the investigation we approached 72 people we were told had lost money to the franchisor. 36 did not respond, 15 said they were happy, and 21 confirmed they’re unhappy.

V/O: Last week Tammy Taylor USA dropped the bomb. They contacted the franchisees on Instagram to say the Viljoens no longer have the right to use the Tammy Taylor trademarks or maintain or grant new franchises. They are aware of counterfeit products being sold and are offering their help.

In an interesting twist, Tammy Taylor Sandton City became the first to jump ship, and announced they will be rebranding to Sweet Escape Beauty.

Happy: It doesn’t make sense, why must I pay for that 2 months rental while they’ve got access to the account? They’re the ones using and misusing the funds in that same account, and they’re misusing the funds deliberately so that I will be left with nothing. V/O: This meant she was now in breach of the handover agreement she’d signed, which meant the Viljoens could reclaim the store. In a written response to Carte Blanche Mel Viljoen states: We have not done or taken anything that Happy did not agree to in writing. Sadly, Happy did not honor her agreement with the brand. Happy Simelane were given ampule time to remedy her breach. (sic) Link: This was supposed to be Happy Simelane’s salon, but after paying R2.8 million in cash, in full, she didn’t even get the keys to the store. The Viljoens took her money and then tried to sell the store to the next buyer. Happy: This is what they do for a living, and you know Peet is just hungry for blood, he’s just going after our money and he’s doing it deliberately and he’s enjoying it. And he thinks he’s untouchable. I want to tell Peet right now you’ve messed with the wrong one. Link: Peet Viljoen will tell anyone who will listen that the R345 000 franchise licence fee is fully refundable. But that’s simply not true. You will not get your refund, well not without a struggle. And if you don’t believe me then listen to Peet Viljoen himself in these astonishing voice recordings were sent to Carte Blanche anonymously. Peet: I don’t think I’ve given back a license fee yet. Mel has behind my back… V/O: These recordings expose Peet’s true nature. Speaking to someone called Lorraine, he admits the promised refund is just a sales pitch. Lorraine: Must you do that? Peet: That’s how they buy, Lorraine. Lorraine: Hmmm? Peet: That’s how they buy. Lorraine: Because they think it’s refundable? Peet: Yes! V/O: He then lashes out at Lorraine for disagreeing. Peet: Fucking bitch, you sell it for me non-refundable! Lorraine: I’m just saying… Peet: No, no please, you’re smart. Give her two sales today, see if she can do it non-refundable. Tell them so. V/O: He goes on to explain his modus operandi. Peet: Right, now I’m going to change one thing that totally puts you, once again in fuck you check mate – it’s the following: when we go from that agreement to this one hey, then when you sign it, it is “no refund”. Peet: Refund expires. But now it’s a contract. And that’s the shit that these dumb, fucking people don’t understand. V/O: But that’s not where the deception ends as our investigation reveals. Link: This is Mel Viljoen’s application for a Protection Order – a desperate attempt to intimidate the media. She asked the court to prohibit Carte Blanche from airing or interviewing or contacting anyone relating to her or her company. The court did not issue the order, yet the Viljoens are claiming that it did. Now if you’ll go to these lengths to try and gag Carte Blanche you probably have something to hide. V/O: Since the Master License Agreement was cancelled the Viljoens have no right to use the name. Tammy Taylor US sent them a Cease & Desist notice, so why have they continued selling franchises and products? We asked both Peet and Mel for an interview, but they referred us to this press release: “The company owned by Melany Viljoen registered the trademark in South Africa. The South African courts do not recognise American law, and the trademark shall remain the property of Melany Viljoen until a South African court rules otherwise.” But that is a lie. V/O: Karel Bredenkamp is a patent attorney specialising in intellectual property. Karel: A company called Just Smart Mobile registered six trademarks for the name Tammy Taylor, or really for logos and including the name Tammy Taylor in the logos. And this was done in June 2016. V/O: Just Smart Mobile belongs to Mel Viljoen. But in 2018 she signed over all her rights to these trademarks to Tammy Taylor US as this Deed of Assignment proves. Karel: So these applications that were filed by Just Smart are now in the name of Tammy Taylor Nails Inc. – in other words the US company. V/O: Tammy Taylor Inc now owns 11 South African trademark registrations and Mel Viljoen owns none. Karel: From this you can see that Tammy Taylor US then filed the word mark – or just the name, the words Tammy Taylor – un-stylized, not as a logo, just Tammy Taylor – and then they also file three logos. Link: Everything you see here from the name, the logo, the products, is Intellectual Property. And it’s the Intellectual Property of Tammy Taylor Incorporated, a company registered in the United States of America. Now since the Master License Agreement between Tammy Taylor US and the Viljoens has been cancelled all of this is a trademark infringement. Karel: The franchisees are exposed. I would strongly suggest that they contact Tammy Taylor US to get authorization again to use the trademarks. V/O: The Distribution Agreement was cancelled in April and Tammy Taylor US no longer supplies the Viljoens. So what fake products are they using? Keystone Cosmetics is an American company, manufacturing nail products at their factory in New Jersey. Their European office is based in the Netherlands, and it’s from here the Viljoens are buying generic products. Here’s an invoice for over 5000 Euros of gels and powders from Keystone Cosmetics. They order through Mel Viljoen’s company called Nectacraft, the same company that was ordering authentic Tammy Taylor products. We called Keystone’s local representative Yvonne to ask about this order. Masa: Are you aware that Nectacraft is actually Tammy Taylor Nails? Yvonne: I don’t answer these types of questions because all our customers are confidential. V/O: An insider revealed the Viljoens are also importing bottles and jars and then rebranding them with fake Tammy Taylor labels. Link: This is an authentic Tammy Taylor Nail Kit from 3 years ago. This is the real thing – manufactured, packaged and labelled in the United States. Everything has got the tammytaylor.com website on it. V/O: But now some of the labels show dot co dot za, while others are clearly not up to scratch as Mel points out to her staff in this leaked video. Mel: The printing is coming off quite hectically. It’s so bad that you can just do this and then, look there! V/O; In another leaked video she places authentic Tammy Taylor jars in front of the fake jars that need labelling. Mel: Please don’t remove these jars that I’ve put there until we’ve got our stickers, otherwise you won’t know what it is. Okay? V/O: So where are labels being printed? Our investigation led us to this warehouse in Midrand. Masa: We just wanted to know did you print these labels, does that artwork look familiar? Guy: Ja, the artwork does look familiar. I’m not sure if it’s the exact artwork because they sent a lot of iterations of it, but we have printed something similar to this. V/O: Further investigation led us to this industrial park in Pretoria. The owner of the Marvel Group showed us some work he’s done for Tammy Taylor. Rudy: Basically what we do is they send us the artwork and we print directly onto the bottles. Masa: Ah, but you see what it says here. You know it still says made in the USA? Rudy: Yeah. Masa: I mean this is not the USA? Rudy: No, not at all. Karel: Well that amounts to trademark infringement, and it also constitutes counterfeiting, because it’s not a product that emanates from Tammy Taylor US. Masa: Just to be clear on this Karel, this is all illegal? Karel: It's all illegal. Counterfeit products could be confiscated and destroyed. V/O: That brings us back to the policemen who arrived at our producer’s gate. Kate: And can I see the other side please? Motau: Which side? Kate: Mr Motau? Oh, Mr Motau which police station are you from? Motau: From Garsfontein. Kate From Garsfontein? Motau: Yes. V/O: Detective Motau is from Pretoria. Sources confirm he was at Tammy Taylor Head Office when a disgruntled franchisee was arrested last year. We played him this video and Motau confirmed he’s the one in the green shirt. But why would this same officer keep turning up? Insiders allege he’s moonlighting. Motau: Alleged? Kate: Yes alleged. Motau: Alleged. Kate: Yes. Motau: You don’t have anything, any proof of anything? Kate: No, it’s alleged. That’s what people do, they make allegations, so I’m asking you. Motau: Those are serious allegations. Kate: Yes, so I’m asking is it true or is it not true? That’s all. Motau: No comment. V/O: During the investigation we approached 72 people we were told had lost money to the franchisor. 36 did not respond, 15 said they were happy, and 21 confirmed they’re unhappy. V/O: Last week Tammy Taylor USA dropped the bomb. They contacted the franchisees on Instagram to say the Viljoens no longer have the right to use the Tammy Taylor trademarks or maintain or grant new franchises. They are aware of counterfeit products being sold and are offering their help. In an interesting twist, Tammy Taylor Sandton City became the first to jump ship, and announced they will be rebranding to Sweet Escape Beauty. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Fake nails, fake products, fake labels - is this the end of the road for Mel and Peet Viljoen and the South African franchise of Tammy Taylor Nails?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Documentary evidence that Peet & Mel Viljoen are no longer License Holders for Tammy Taylor Nails, and that their Distribution Agreement has not been renewed. However, they still have 40+ Tammy Taylor Salons operating in Southern Africa, which are now infringing on the Tammy Taylor trademark which is registered to Tammy Taylor Inc. (A company registered in the USA). Not only are their investments and their livelihoods at stake, but they are knowingly or unknowingly selling fake products which have not been procured from Tammy Taylor USA. For the past year Mel & Peet Viljoen have been importing products (gels. powders, etc) from the Netherlands, and bottles and containers from China. These are then re-branded with Tammy Taylor labels printed in Pretoria. We have invoices proving the purchase as well as a video of Mel examining a peeling fake label.
metadata.Summary: Peet Viljoen also contracted with Tahera Mather (Digital Vibes) to supply 80 000 face masks to the Department of Health and 20 000 to SAPS in 2020. He was paid R5.1 million for these by Spin Wizards, a company implicated in the Digital Vibes saga which saw the former Minister Zweli Mkhize stepping down. Peet then made a big splash in every local newspaper about donating 1000 masks to the police. Masks paid for handsomely by the Department of Health's communication budget. The SIU Report also details how R650 000 of this budget was diverted to Minister Mkhize's daughter-in-law to open a new Tammy Taylor Nail salon in Pietermaritzburg's Midlands Mall.
metadata.Further information: Entrepreneur and influencer Happy Simelane paid R2.8 million for the Tammy Taylor Menlyn Maine store in August 2021. She was presented with a set of fake financials by Peet, drawn up by his 'accountant'. This shows the monthly rental as R21 000 per month. In reality the rental is R62 597 per month. Happy never received a set of keys to the shop, and the business was only transferred into her name on 12 October 2021. Nevertheless she received a letter of demand from Peet for 2 months rental (September & October 2021) totalling about R150 000. According to the franchise agreement if the rental is 2 months in arrears they can take back the store. Which they did, and Happy lost her R2.8 million. In addition to this her husband was killed in a car accident in June this year. She is taking them to court.
